purpose: Sourced scalar thermal conductivity and reciprocal resistivity for soil heat-transfer inputs and CPU/GPU arithmetic validation.
scope: No cable ampacity, approved rating, restoration recommendation or site property is inferred. Anisotropic tensors are outside this scalar contract.

conductivity.validation: finite real number > 0; reject booleans and missing values

source.meaning: Nonempty citation/DOI and sample identifier, model input provenance, or explicit synthetic scenario identifier

model.meaning: Model identifier/version; document calibration and applicability outside this arithmetic converter

conditions.meaning: Preserve known measurement/model conditions. Explicit null means unknown and prevents pretending conditions match a cable trench.

volumetric_water_content.meaning: Liquid water volume / bulk soil volume; distinct from mass water content

gravimetric_water_content_dry_basis.meaning: Water mass / dry soil mass; wet-basis content must be separately labelled

dry_bulk_density.meaning: Dry solid mass / bulk sample volume; distinguish fine-earth fraction and whole soil

temperature.meaning: Measurement/model temperature; record frozen or unfrozen state

depth_bottom.meaning: Below ground level; not inferred from topsoil data

method.meaning: Measurement method, instrument, sample preparation and compaction where available

mineralogy_texture_organic_matter.meaning: Covariates only; no built-in conversion to conductivity

unit_rules: Thermal resistivity K m/W is not electrical resistivity ohm m.
Hydraulic conductivity m/s is a different quantity from thermal conductivity W/(m K).
A temperature difference of one degree Celsius equals one kelvin; 100 degC cm/W = 1 K m/W.
Bulk density 1 g/cm3 = 1000 kg/m3. Percent moisture requires division by 100 and an explicit wet-mass, dry-mass or volume basis.
Do not convert unknown/no-data conductivity to zero or silently fill a nominal conductivity.
For positive conductivity interval [k_low,k_high], reciprocal bounds are [1/k_high,1/k_low]; inverse(mean(k)) is not generally mean(1/k).
interpretation: Moisture, dry density and composition affect thermal properties; an unconditioned soil class is not a measured thermal property.
Retain seasonal conditions, drying history and possible heat-driven moisture redistribution. The converter itself models none of these.
A model requires calibration/application-domain evidence. Soil moisture and density datasets can supply covariates but cannot alone establish site thermal conductivity.
Cable thermal calculations additionally require cable construction, losses, arrangement, burial depth and thermal boundary conditions; this contract provides no ampacity result.
